corrected_verdict: KNOWN. lem:avg is Morwani et al. (ICLR 2024) Sec. 3.2's inequality g' >= g, with q uniform on D_p, tau(x,y) the point mass on y - delta, and the expectation summed over neurons (Sec. 3.2 already writes it neuron by neuron). Morwani App. I Eq. (10) already uses averaged margins weighted by offset (sum_{c != e} tau_c h(c)). So choosing weights per offset is not a departure either. The min over delta belongs to later items, not to this lemma. Credit Sec. 3.2 and App. F.1 (confirmed in v2), and do not present lem:avg as a contribution.
issues:
Search limits: the WebSearch budget was already exhausted (200/200). The arXiv export API and the Semantic Scholar search API mostly returned HTTP 429, and DuckDuckGo showed a CAPTCHA. Coverage came from:
- the arXiv web search, about 12 queries before it was rate-limited;
- the Semantic Scholar list of papers citing 2311.07568 (40 papers);

So coverage of the 2025-26 arXiv is partial. The verdict does not depend on that, because the lemma is a one-line specialisation of a published statement.

Citation check: morwani2024feature is confirmed.
- arXiv abs metadata gives the title, the 5 authors and "Spotlight at ICLR 2024".
- OpenReview API note i9wDX850jR gives venue "ICLR 2024 spotlight".
- Both of the checker's pointer fixes are correct in v2: Sec. 3.2 defines g' and says "g' >= g as g' replaces the max by a weighted sum"; App. F.1 defines eta_{u,v,w}(delta), with Eq. (4) using uniform tau = 1/(p-1).

Corrections to the checker:
- The checker says "The only difference: we use a point-mass tau at each offset instead of a uniform tau". That understates Morwani.
  - App. I Eq. (10): "h_{u,v,w}(e) - sum_{c != e} tau_c h_{u,v,w}(c), where sum tau_c = 1" is a margin weighted by offset.
  - Lemma 19 deliberately picks a non-uniform tau_{C_n} = sum_R z_R chi_R(C_n), because uniform weights would select only the sign representation.
  - For abelian groups, a point mass at delta is an admissible tau. Caveat: App. I assumes real representations, so Z_p is not literally covered.
- The checker's optional clause "Morwani et al. use a uniform weighting over wrong labels" is wrong as a blanket statement. It holds only for modular addition (App. F.1). Scope it to that case if it is added.

Prior art the checker missed (not new against the paper, but relevant):
- Li et al. (AISTATS 2025, arXiv 2402.09469), Def. 3.6, restates the class-weighted margin for k-input modular addition. They also note g <= g' and use uniform tau (App. D). This is the n-operand precedent for the same device, and it is already in the bib as li2025nsum.

Adversarial candidates checked, none with a per-offset margin bound: 2407.12332, 2602.16849, 2511.23443, 2410.07476, 2608.04451, 2602.03655, 2410.01779, 2509.21519, 2604.00316, 2506.06489.
- 2602.16849 (He et al.) has only the uniform average margin.
- 2410.07476 gives per-input lower bounds on the margin, used for verification.

Cross-item flags for the orchestrator:
- R3 (phase lemma / coverage): Morwani Lemma 16/18 has the coefficient [1 - sum_n tau_{C_n}|C_n| chi_R(C_n)/d_R]. With a point-mass tau at delta and the 2-dim real rep of Z_p (chi = 2cos, d = 2), this equals 1 - cos(2 pi j delta/p), which is our coverage. It should be credited there.
- R8/dual: Lemma 19's tau, which equalises all irreps, is the dual-optimal offset weighting at b = nu.
- R2: Morwani App. F.3 already uses the diagonal Fourier coefficients f-hat(j,k,l) with j = k = -l as the per-frequency signature.
